title: app-14: Startup diagnostics — one list of what fell back, and a marker that stays until it is fixed
summary: Everything that goes wrong while heca loads (config, theme, program catalog, keybindings, plugins) collects into one rebuilt-per-load list with a severity and an origin; a status-bar marker shows it, a log file carries the detail for a plugin author, and RPC can read it. Never blocks startup.
description:
**Decided with Antonio, 2026-08-11.** The trigger was T335 ("a contributed keybinding that loses a collision is dropped silently"), but the discussion showed that is one producer of a much larger hole.

## The problem, stated once

**Everything that can go wrong while heca is starting up currently goes to `eprintln!` in a debug build, and nowhere else.** A mistyped key in `config.toml`, a theme that failed to load, a malformed `[program]` entry, a plugin keybinding refused by a collision, a plugin that failed to mount. Run from a terminal you might catch some of it scrolling past; **run as an OS app — which is where heca is going — and you see none of it.** The app simply, quietly, is not what the user asked for.

Antonio, 2026-08-11: *"now we run the app via terminal, later we will add it as a OS app. we need a way to show the misconfiguration on start up."*

**And a new plugin needs a restart** — the WASM module has to be loaded and its actions/regions registered before anything can use them. So startup is *a* moment problems appear. It is not the only one: `prefix+Shift+r` (`WmAction::ReloadConfig`, `reload_config()`) rebuilds keymaps, theme and settings without a restart, so the same class of problem appears there too.

## The two decisions

1. **Never block startup.** Anything broken **falls back to its default and is reported**. A modal at launch would mean the app cannot start over a typo. (Antonio: *"always fall back to defaults and report"*.)
2. **The marker stays until the problem is actually gone** — not dismissible. Dismissing a warning about a config you have not fixed just hides it. (Antonio: *"marker stays until fixed"*.)

**The consequence of (2), and the thing to get right:** the list is **rebuilt on every load and reload, never appended to.** It is a view of *what is wrong right now*, not a history. Otherwise fixing a setting leaves its old entry behind and the marker never clears — which would make the marker worthless within a week.

## The shape: one collector, several producers, three readers

**One collector.** A diagnostics list on `AppState`, filled during load and refilled by `reload_config()`. Each entry carries: a **severity** (fell back to a default / could not be applied at all), an **origin** (which file, which key, which plugin), and a **message written for the person who can fix it**.

**Producers that already exist and are waiting for somewhere to report:**
- `register_component_keybinding` (`heca/src/app/registry.rs`) — a contributed binding refused because the config already bound that combo or rebound that action. **This is T335**, whose only remaining scope is this call.
- Config loading (`heca-config/src/loader.rs`) — a value that failed to parse and fell back.
- Theme / program-catalog load.
- Plugin mount failures (F003/P022, when it exists).

**Three readers, because they are three different people:**
- **The user** — a small persistent marker in the status bar ("2 problems"), which opens the list. **Not a toast**: a toast is for something that just happened while you work; this is a *state the app is in*. Not a modal, per decision (1).
- **The plugin author** — a **log file** with the full detail. A one-line banner is useless to them: they need to know *which* binding lost to *which* combo, on a machine that is not theirs.
- **RPC** — so it is scriptable, and so a test can assert a clean start.

## Why this is NOT part of F009 🔔 Notification System

A notification is an event: something happened, here is a transient message. This is the opposite — a **standing condition** that persists until the config changes. Filing it as a notification producer is what left T335 and P055(F009)/T381 waiting on a feature with 60 unstarted tasks, and it would also be noisy in practice: a reload that drops five bindings would fire five toasts.

They are compatible, not competing. When F009 lands it can render a **summary** of this list ("2 problems at startup") as one notification, which is one producer reading one collector — the DRY shape. **This phase does not wait on F009.**

⚠️ F010 (Improvements) carries a note about "notify about blocked keybindings" — the same thing, tracked in a second place. Fold it in here.

## Behaviours to preserve

- **Startup never fails because of user input.** The existing fallback behaviour (embedded `config.default.toml` ⊕ `keybindings.default.toml`, deep-merged with the user's files) is correct and stays; this phase only makes the fallbacks *visible*.
- **Config wins a keybinding collision.** Settled and shipped (`Provider::keybindings()`, `heca/src/providers/mod.rs:196`); this phase reports the loss, it does not change who wins.
- **The status bar is a widget**, so the marker is a composed widget reading a signal — not a hand-drawn glyph, and not a bespoke surface. `AGENTS.md` § "Creating new widgets" applies.
- **The list surface is a described tree** where it can be, so the same rule the rest of the chrome follows holds: one path, and a plugin's diagnostics render like the host's.

tasks.title: The collector: one diagnostics list, rebuilt on every load and reload
tasks.description:
The foundation every other task in this phase reads or writes. Nothing user-facing.

## What to build

A diagnostics list on `AppState`, holding entries of roughly:

- **severity** — "fell back to a default" vs "could not be applied at all". Two levels, not five: the question a reader asks is only *did heca do what I asked, or something else*.
- **origin** — which file and which key (`config.toml [settings] window_wdith`), or which plugin and which action. Enough for the person who can fix it to find it.
- **message** — written for that person, not for the log.

## The invariant that decides the design

**It is rebuilt on every load and refilled on every reload — never appended to.** It is a view of *what is wrong right now*, not a history. Antonio's decision that the marker "stays until fixed" only works if fixing a setting removes its entry: otherwise the old entry survives the fix and the marker never clears.

So: `reload_config()` (`heca/src/app/*`, reached by `WmAction::ReloadConfig` / `prefix+Shift+r`) clears the list before it re-reads, exactly as it rebuilds the keymaps.

## Where the producers are

- `register_component_keybinding` (`heca/src/app/registry.rs`) — returns early when the `BindingIndex` already knows the action, and skips a combo the layer already resolves. Both of those early returns are a refusal that is currently silent. This is the whole remaining scope of **P080(F003)/T335**.
- `heca-config/src/loader.rs` — the deep-merge of embedded defaults ⊕ `~/.config/heca/config.toml` ⊕ `~/.config/heca/keybindings.toml`. A value that fails to parse and falls back is invisible today.
- Theme and `[program]` catalog load.
- Plugin mount, when F003/P022 exists.

## Edge cases

- **A problem that recurs on reload must not double.** It is a fresh list each time, so this falls out of the invariant rather than needing a dedup rule — but a test should hold it.
- **Startup order.** Config loads before the window exists; the list has to live somewhere that outlives that, so collect into it before `AppState` is assembled and hand it over, rather than reaching for `AppState` from the loader.
- **`heca-config` must not depend on the app** to report. The loader returns its problems with the config it parsed; the app files them. Same boundary rule as everywhere else.

## Behaviour to preserve

**Startup never fails because of user input.** The fallback behaviour is correct and stays; this only makes it visible.

tasks.title: The marker and the list — what the user sees, and it does not go away until the config is fixed
tasks.description:
The user-facing half. Depends on the collector (T410).

## What to build

A small **persistent marker in the status bar** — "2 problems" — that opens the diagnostics list. Reads a signal off the collector, so it appears, updates and **disappears on its own** when a reload clears the list.

**Not dismissible.** Antonio, 2026-08-11: *"marker stays until fixed"*. Dismissing a warning about a config you have not fixed just hides it; fixing the config and reloading is what clears it.

**Not a toast, and not a modal.** A toast is for something that just happened while you work; this is a *state the app is in*, which is why it persists and why one entry per problem would be noise. A modal is ruled out by the phase's first decision — startup never blocks.

## Rules this must follow

- **The status bar is a widget**, so the marker is a composed widget reading a signal — not a hand-drawn glyph in `render.rs`, and not a bespoke surface. Run the PRE-FLIGHT (`AGENTS.md` §0) first: `Badge` / `Tag` / `StatusDot` / `Row` almost certainly cover it, and if they do not, it is a proper generic widget in `heca-grid-ui`, never inline `Flex`+`Surface` with hardcoded colours.
- **The list surface is a described tree** where it can be, so the same one path the rest of the chrome uses holds and a plugin's diagnostics render like the host's. See F003 and P067.
- **Opening it is an action**, so it is reachable from the mouse, a keybinding and RPC — not trapped behind clicking the marker. Follow the "Adding New Actions" checklist, including the declared `args` step and the `ActionPolicy` classification (`Global` — reading a diagnostics list has no layout impact and must work while a pane is floating).

## Edge cases

- **Zero problems** ⇒ no marker at all, not a green tick. The bar is crowded and a permanent "everything is fine" indicator earns nothing.
- **The list is open when a reload clears it** — it should empty in place, not close under the user.
- **Many entries** — the list scrolls (`ScrollRegion`); it does not truncate silently, which would be the same defect this phase exists to fix.

tasks.title: The log file and the RPC read — the plugin author's channel, and the scriptable one
tasks.description:
The other two readers of the collector (T410). A one-line marker serves the user; it is useless to the two audiences below.

## The log file — for the plugin author

A plugin author needs the **full detail**, on a machine that is not theirs: *which* binding lost to *which* combo, which action was already bound, which file the winning binding came from. They will never see a status-bar marker, because they are not the one running the app.

So the collector also writes a log on every load and reload. Detail here, not brevity — this is the one place where verbosity is correct.

**Today this is `eprintln!` under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`**, which means it exists only in a debug build and only if the app was launched from a terminal. Both of those stop being true when heca ships as an OS app, which is the reason this phase exists.

## The RPC read

Expose the list over RPC so it is **scriptable**, and so **a test can assert a clean start** — which is the part that keeps this honest over time. A regression that adds a silent fallback should fail a test, not wait to be noticed.

Follow the "Adding New Actions" checklist: declared `args`, an `ActionPolicy` classification (`Global` — reading diagnostics has no layout impact), and RPC parser support. Metadata is then discoverable through the existing `list-actions` / `describe-action` introspection with nothing further.

## Edge cases

- **Where the log goes** must work for a double-clicked OS app, not only a terminal launch — the platform's log directory, not the working directory.
- **The log is rewritten per load, like the list**, or it is a log with rotation. Pick one deliberately; an append-forever file in a config directory is a slow leak.
- **No secrets.** The log names files and keys; it should not dump whole config contents, which may hold command lines a user would not want written out.
